messages:
maria: Morning handoff — quick summary of the overnight/early-morning activity and what I'm leaving you with. TL;DR: primary pager for eu-west kv-evictions triggered ~02:14 UTC, several customer-facing 503s for short windows, mitigations applied (fallback routing + soft throttle), currently stable but reduced capacity in eu-west. Full timeline below.

maria: Who's primary for the next block? @kevin you said you'd take primary for the day, right? If so, pls confirm and I'll hand secondary to @aj.

kevin: I can take primary for the next 8h. I'll be reachable on pager and +1 on slack. handing secondary to aj sounds good.

aj: Taking secondary. I'll monitor embed/kv dashboards and be ready to swap if capacity drops.

maria: Incident details — root cause and actions: we saw KV eviction rate spike on a small subset of eu-west nodes after a config change to eviction thresholds deployed at ~01:58 UTC (deploybot: deployment 2026.03.15/kv-config-v3). Evictions cascaded into request tails and some routers hit capacity and returned 503s.

oncall-bot: [INCIDENT] Pager triggered: kv-evictions-eu-west (P1) @02:14 UTC — 7 pages total, 3 acknowledged. Link: https://redwood.ops/incident/INC-20260315-42

maria: What we did:
- rolled back kv-config change (deploybot rollback initiated at 02:25 UTC)
- applied routing soft-fallback to regional standby pool (automated)
- tightened client throttles for long-tail requests for 20m windows
- kicked off eviction-heap-scan on affected nodes (runbook step 3)
Result: eviction rate declined to baseline by ~02:40 UTC, request success rate restored.

sasha: Customer impact summary: two customers saw brief errors — CustomerA (API) and PartnerX (embedding sync). CustomerA reported ~2m of 503s, PartnerX had retries that caused backlog but no data loss. I opened tickets and assigned to support for outreach.

maria: Current status:
- eu-west cluster: stable but at 75% effective capacity (we've drained some nodes for heap scan).
- No active pages.
- Canary traffic back to normal routes.
- Observability: p95 latency returned to normal, token generation p99 still slightly elevated for long requests.

kevin: Any remaining manual tasks?

maria: Yes — three follow-ups before EOD: 
1) Confirm eviction threshold config that rolled back is reverted in prod config repo and add extra guardrail (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra/PR-4321). Owner: @maria.
2) Run a targeted soak on drained nodes overnight and collect heap/eviction metrics (runbook link: https://redwood.runbooks/kv-eviction). Owner: @aj.
3) Customer comms: support to send incident summary and RC to CustomerA and PartnerX. Owner: @sasha.

aj: Noted. I'll schedule the soak — ETA 6h from now and will paste results here.

maria: Risk/coverage notes:
- Coverage gap: no on-call in apac nights today (weekend rota) — if problem reappears, regional fallback to us-west is enabled but will increase latency for APAC customers. If pages fire and I can't respond, escalate to kevin primary.
- Known flaky router ids: rtr-eu-12 and rtr-eu-09 (we put them in maintenance).

kevin: I'll add a short alert filter to reduce noise for non-actionable kv-saturation alerts for next 4h. If anything RAISES to P1, I'll slack the incidents channel and call list.

maria: Runbook pointers (short):
- kv-eviction triage: runbook step 1->4: https://redwood.runbooks/kv-eviction
- rolling rollback commands: ```deploybot rollback infra/kv-config-v3 --target eu-west```
- traffic reroute check: `curl https://ops-api/redwood/routes?region=eu-west`

oncall-bot: [DEPLOY] rollback completed by maria at 02:26 UTC — build 2026.03.15-kv-config-v2 restored.

sasha: Quick note on monitoring: I added a temporary dashboard with eviction_rate, router_queue_len, p99.token_latency for eu-west and shared with this thread. link: https://monitoring.redwood/d/eviction-eu-west

maria: Next steps for incoming shift (kevin primary / aj secondary):
- Monitor the dashboard closely for the next 6h.
- Keep an eye on router queue length — if >200 for 5m, execute step 2 of runbook (increase standby capacity + throttle).
- If pages fire, follow the escalation checklist in runbook and update thread.

kevin: Got it. I'll watch and post any anomalies here.

aj: Will post soak results and any heap dump snippets if we see related OOMs.

maria: Thanks team — handing off. Leaving relevant links in the incident ticket and will be available on slack if needed. :wave:

kevin: Thanks, taking over. :thumbsup:
